Biopsies were incubated at 37°C for 20-30 minutes with mixing using a 5-10 mL serological pipet and intermittent gentle vortexing at 2-5-minute intervals. The extent of tumor tissue dissociation was variable and likely dependent on extracellular matrix abundance. The resulting cell suspension was passed through a 70 um nylon mesh filter and washed with an additional 5-10 mL of RPMI media. !Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Single cell
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: Post-Tx
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Fresh tumor tissue was transferred to a 6 cm tissue culture dish in a small volume of DMEM media and cut into <2 mm pieces with a razor blade. Tissue pieces were centrifuged (400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C for all centrifuge steps) and resuspended in 2-5 mL of a collagenase-containing enzymatic digestion solution (Miltenyi Human Tumor Dissociation Kit #30-095-929), based on the weight of collected tissue, according to manufacturer’s instructions. Biopsies were incubated at 37°C for 20-30 minutes with mixing using a 5-10 mL serological pipet and intermittent gentle vortexing at 2-5-minute intervals. The extent of tumor tissue dissociation was variable and likely dependent on extracellular matrix abundance. The resulting cell suspension was passed through a 70 um nylon mesh filter and washed with an additional 5-10 mL of RPMI media. Filtered tumor cell suspensions were centrifuged and resuspended in 3 mL ACK red blood cell lysis buffer (Gibco #A1049201) for 1 minute at RT, then immediately diluted with 10 mL of PBS (Life Technologies #10437028). Cells were pelleted and resuspended in Zombie NIR (Biolegend) viability dye solution (1:500 in PBS), followed by a 15 minute incubation at RT in the dark. Cells were counted with a hemocytometer, yielding on average 1.3x104 live cells/mg of tumor tissue. Up to 500,000 live cells were then resuspended in 100 uL of FACS wash buffer (FWB; PBS, 2% FBS, 1 mM EDTA) with the addition of the following antibodies: TruStain FcX (Biolegend 422302), CD3-PE/Dazzle (Biolegend 300450), CD45-Pacific Blue (Biolegend 304022), CD66b-PE/Cy7 (Biolegend 305116) and CD15-APC (Biolegend 301908). Cells were incubated on ice for 20 minutes, washed with 1 mL FWB, filtered through 40 um flow-cap strainers, and then resuspended in 500 uL FWB. Cells were sorted using a FACS Aria II or III instrument (BD Biosciences). For most samples, 12-15 x 103 live CD45+CD66b- mononuclear cells (MNC) cells were sorted into T cell media (RPMI + 10% FBS) and immediately transferred to ice. All scRNA-seq was performed using the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 assay and protocols (10x Genomics). CD45+ cells isolated as above were centrifuged and washed with PBS containing 0.05% RNase-free BSA (ThermoFisher Scientific #AM2616), leaving a volume of <32 uL after the final wash. Up to 15,000 cells based on cell sorter count were loaded into a Single Cell Chip A channel, along with reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.

Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. !Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.

!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: TCR: b chains
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Bulk
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: Pre-Tx
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor b chains
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) sections.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.

!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.

!Sample_supplementary_file_1 = ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/samples/GSM6048nnn/GSM6048213/suppl/GSM6048213_P07_post-Tx_TCR_bulk_tumor.tsv.gz
!Sample_series_id = GSE200996
!Sample_data_row_count = 0
^SAMPLE = GSM6048214
!Sample_title = P08 bulk TCR of post-Tx HNSCC tumor
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6048214
!Sample_status = Public on Jul 07 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 18 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Jul 07 2022
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC tumor
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: TCR: b chains
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Bulk
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: Post-Tx
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor b chains
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) sections.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) sections.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.

!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = PBMCs isolated as described above were thawed in groups in 5-6 vials at a time, with each vial representing an individual blood draw. Thawed PBMCS were immediately diluted into 10 mL PBS, centrifuged (400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C for all centrifugation steps) and resuspended in PBS. Cells were counted with a hemacytometer; viability of thawed cells averaged 55%. Live cells were sorted to ensure the quality of scRNA-seq libraries. Between 0.5-1x10^6 cells were stained with Zombie NIR (Biolegend) diluted 1:500 in PBS for 15 minutes at RT. Cells were centrifuged and then resuspended in 90 uL of FWB, to which the following were added: 5 uL of TruStain Fx FcBlock (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD45-Pacific Blue (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD3-PE/Dazzle594 (Biolegend) and 2 uL (1 ug) of a TotalSeqC hashing antibody (Biolegend). For each group of up to six PBMC vials, unique hashtags were used for later identification of cells from individual samples. Cells were incubated for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with 500 uL FWB, and filtered through 40 um flow-cap strainers. Live CD45+ cells (50,000 to 100,000 cells) were then separately sorted using a FACS Aria II instrument for each hashtag-labeled sample. Cells were sorted into 500 uL 0.1% BSA in 1.5 mL DNA LoBind microcentrifuge tubes (Eppendorf). Following sorting, cells were centrifuged, washed with 0.25% BSA, and resuspended in a final volume of 30-50 uL 0.25% BSA. Live cells were counted with a hemacytometer. For generation of single-cell emulsions, 6000 live cells from each sample (up to six samples) were pooled and loaded into a single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads, according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 manufacturer’s protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX, feature barcode, and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)
!Sample_description = hashtag_info_sc_GEX_PBMC.csv
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: CD45+
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Single cell
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B1/B2/B3
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: total RNA
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = PBMCs isolated as described above were thawed in groups in 5-6 vials at a time, with each vial representing an individual blood draw. Thawed PBMCS were immediately diluted into 10 mL PBS, centrifuged (400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C for all centrifugation steps) and resuspended in PBS. Cells were counted with a hemacytometer; viability of thawed cells averaged 55%. Live cells were sorted to ensure the quality of scRNA-seq libraries. Between 0.5-1x10^6 cells were stained with Zombie NIR (Biolegend) diluted 1:500 in PBS for 15 minutes at RT. Cells were centrifuged and then resuspended in 90 uL of FWB, to which the following were added: 5 uL of TruStain Fx FcBlock (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD45-Pacific Blue (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD3-PE/Dazzle594 (Biolegend) and 2 uL (1 ug) of a TotalSeqC hashing antibody (Biolegend). For each group of up to six PBMC vials, unique hashtags were used for later identification of cells from individual samples. Cells were incubated for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with 500 uL FWB, and filtered through 40 um flow-cap strainers. Live CD45+ cells (50,000 to 100,000 cells) were then separately sorted using a FACS Aria II instrument for each hashtag-labeled sample. Cells were sorted into 500 uL 0.1% BSA in 1.5 mL DNA LoBind microcentrifuge tubes (Eppendorf). Following sorting, cells were centrifuged, washed with 0.25% BSA, and resuspended in a final volume of 30-50 uL 0.25% BSA. Live cells were counted with a hemacytometer. For generation of single-cell emulsions, 6000 live cells from each sample (up to six samples) were pooled and loaded into a single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads, according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 manufacturer’s protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX, feature barcode, and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)

We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = PBMCs isolated as described above were thawed in groups in 5-6 vials at a time, with each vial representing an individual blood draw. Thawed PBMCS were immediately diluted into 10 mL PBS, centrifuged (400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C for all centrifugation steps) and resuspended in PBS. Cells were counted with a hemacytometer; viability of thawed cells averaged 55%. Live cells were sorted to ensure the quality of scRNA-seq libraries. Between 0.5-1x10^6 cells were stained with Zombie NIR (Biolegend) diluted 1:500 in PBS for 15 minutes at RT. Cells were centrifuged and then resuspended in 90 uL of FWB, to which the following were added: 5 uL of TruStain Fx FcBlock (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD45-Pacific Blue (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD3-PE/Dazzle594 (Biolegend) and 2 uL (1 ug) of a TotalSeqC hashing antibody (Biolegend). For each group of up to six PBMC vials, unique hashtags were used for later identification of cells from individual samples. Cells were incubated for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with 500 uL FWB, and filtered through 40 um flow-cap strainers. Live CD45+ cells (50,000 to 100,000 cells) were then separately sorted using a FACS Aria II instrument for each hashtag-labeled sample. Cells were sorted into 500 uL 0.1% BSA in 1.5 mL DNA LoBind microcentrifuge tubes (Eppendorf). Following sorting, cells were centrifuged, washed with 0.25% BSA, and resuspended in a final volume of 30-50 uL 0.25% BSA. Live cells were counted with a hemacytometer. For generation of single-cell emulsions, 6000 live cells from each sample (up to six samples) were pooled and loaded into a single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads, according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 manufacturer’s protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX, feature barcode, and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)

!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.

Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. !Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = PBMCs isolated as described above were thawed in groups in 5-6 vials at a time, with each vial representing an individual blood draw. Thawed PBMCS were immediately diluted into 10 mL PBS, centrifuged (400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C for all centrifugation steps) and resuspended in PBS. Cells were counted with a hemacytometer; viability of thawed cells averaged 55%. Live cells were sorted to ensure the quality of scRNA-seq libraries. Between 0.5-1x10^6 cells were stained with Zombie NIR (Biolegend) diluted 1:500 in PBS for 15 minutes at RT. Cells were centrifuged and then resuspended in 90 uL of FWB, to which the following were added: 5 uL of TruStain Fx FcBlock (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD45-Pacific Blue (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD3-PE/Dazzle594 (Biolegend) and 2 uL (1 ug) of a TotalSeqC hashing antibody (Biolegend). For each group of up to six PBMC vials, unique hashtags were used for later identification of cells from individual samples. Cells were incubated for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with 500 uL FWB, and filtered through 40 um flow-cap strainers. Live CD45+ cells (50,000 to 100,000 cells) were then separately sorted using a FACS Aria II instrument for each hashtag-labeled sample. Cells were sorted into 500 uL 0.1% BSA in 1.5 mL DNA LoBind microcentrifuge tubes (Eppendorf). Following sorting, cells were centrifuged, washed with 0.25% BSA, and resuspended in a final volume of 30-50 uL 0.25% BSA. Live cells were counted with a hemacytometer. For generation of single-cell emulsions, 6000 live cells from each sample (up to six samples) were pooled and loaded into a single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads, according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 manufacturer’s protocol.

!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. !Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Single cell
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B1/B2/B3

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = PBMCs isolated as described above were thawed in groups in 5-6 vials at a time, with each vial representing an individual blood draw. Thawed PBMCS were immediately diluted into 10 mL PBS, centrifuged (400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C for all centrifugation steps) and resuspended in PBS. Cells were counted with a hemacytometer; viability of thawed cells averaged 55%. Live cells were sorted to ensure the quality of scRNA-seq libraries. Between 0.5-1x10^6 cells were stained with Zombie NIR (Biolegend) diluted 1:500 in PBS for 15 minutes at RT. Cells were centrifuged and then resuspended in 90 uL of FWB, to which the following were added: 5 uL of TruStain Fx FcBlock (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD45-Pacific Blue (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD3-PE/Dazzle594 (Biolegend) and 2 uL (1 ug) of a TotalSeqC hashing antibody (Biolegend). For each group of up to six PBMC vials, unique hashtags were used for later identification of cells from individual samples. Cells were incubated for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with 500 uL FWB, and filtered through 40 um flow-cap strainers. Live CD45+ cells (50,000 to 100,000 cells) were then separately sorted using a FACS Aria II instrument for each hashtag-labeled sample. Cells were sorted into 500 uL 0.1% BSA in 1.5 mL DNA LoBind microcentrifuge tubes (Eppendorf). Following sorting, cells were centrifuged, washed with 0.25% BSA, and resuspended in a final volume of 30-50 uL 0.25% BSA. Live cells were counted with a hemacytometer. For generation of single-cell emulsions, 6000 live cells from each sample (up to six samples) were pooled and loaded into a single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads, according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 manufacturer’s protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX, feature barcode, and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.

!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_supplementary_file_1 = ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/samples/GSM6048nnn/GSM6048251/suppl/GSM6048251_filtered_contig_annotations_P13-P14_TCR_sc_PBMC.csv.gz

^SAMPLE = GSM6048252
!Sample_title = P15 and P17 single cell TCR of HNSCC PBMC (Hashtag)
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6048252
!Sample_status = Public on Jul 07 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 18 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Jul 07 2022
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: TCR: ab chains
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Single cell
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B1/B2/B3
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = PBMCs isolated as described above were thawed in groups in 5-6 vials at a time, with each vial representing an individual blood draw. Thawed PBMCS were immediately diluted into 10 mL PBS, centrifuged (400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C for all centrifugation steps) and resuspended in PBS. Cells were counted with a hemacytometer; viability of thawed cells averaged 55%. Live cells were sorted to ensure the quality of scRNA-seq libraries. Between 0.5-1x10^6 cells were stained with Zombie NIR (Biolegend) diluted 1:500 in PBS for 15 minutes at RT. Cells were centrifuged and then resuspended in 90 uL of FWB, to which the following were added: 5 uL of TruStain Fx FcBlock (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD45-Pacific Blue (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD3-PE/Dazzle594 (Biolegend) and 2 uL (1 ug) of a TotalSeqC hashing antibody (Biolegend). For each group of up to six PBMC vials, unique hashtags were used for later identification of cells from individual samples. Cells were incubated for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with 500 uL FWB, and filtered through 40 um flow-cap strainers. Live CD45+ cells (50,000 to 100,000 cells) were then separately sorted using a FACS Aria II instrument for each hashtag-labeled sample. Cells were sorted into 500 uL 0.1% BSA in 1.5 mL DNA LoBind microcentrifuge tubes (Eppendorf). Following sorting, cells were centrifuged, washed with 0.25% BSA, and resuspended in a final volume of 30-50 uL 0.25% BSA. Live cells were counted with a hemacytometer. For generation of single-cell emulsions, 6000 live cells from each sample (up to six samples) were pooled and loaded into a single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads, according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 manufacturer’s protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX, feature barcode, and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.

For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_title = P21, P25 and P28 single cell TCR of HNSCC PBMC (Hashtag)
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6048256
!Sample_status = Public on Jul 07 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 18 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Jul 07 2022
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: TCR: ab chains
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Single cell
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B1/B2/B3
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = PBMCs isolated as described above were thawed in groups in 5-6 vials at a time, with each vial representing an individual blood draw. Thawed PBMCS were immediately diluted into 10 mL PBS, centrifuged (400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C for all centrifugation steps) and resuspended in PBS. Cells were counted with a hemacytometer; viability of thawed cells averaged 55%. Live cells were sorted to ensure the quality of scRNA-seq libraries. Between 0.5-1x10^6 cells were stained with Zombie NIR (Biolegend) diluted 1:500 in PBS for 15 minutes at RT. Cells were centrifuged and then resuspended in 90 uL of FWB, to which the following were added: 5 uL of TruStain Fx FcBlock (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD45-Pacific Blue (Biolegend), 2 uL of aCD3-PE/Dazzle594 (Biolegend) and 2 uL (1 ug) of a TotalSeqC hashing antibody (Biolegend). For each group of up to six PBMC vials, unique hashtags were used for later identification of cells from individual samples. Cells were incubated for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with 500 uL FWB, and filtered through 40 um flow-cap strainers. Live CD45+ cells (50,000 to 100,000 cells) were then separately sorted using a FACS Aria II instrument for each hashtag-labeled sample. Cells were sorted into 500 uL 0.1% BSA in 1.5 mL DNA LoBind microcentrifuge tubes (Eppendorf). Following sorting, cells were centrifuged, washed with 0.25% BSA, and resuspended in a final volume of 30-50 uL 0.25% BSA. Live cells were counted with a hemacytometer. For generation of single-cell emulsions, 6000 live cells from each sample (up to six samples) were pooled and loaded into a single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads, according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 manufacturer’s protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX, feature barcode, and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.

!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B1
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor b chains
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Between 0.5-2.0 x106 PBMCs were pelleted and snap-frozen on dry-ice. Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from cell pellets.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.
