!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.

!Sample_library_strategy = RNA-Seq
!Sample_supplementary_file_1 = ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/samples/GSM6048nnn/GSM6048270/suppl/GSM6048270_P14_B1_TCR_bulk_PBMC.tsv.gz
!Sample_series_id = GSE200996
!Sample_data_row_count = 0
^SAMPLE = GSM6048271
!Sample_title = P15 bulk TCR of B1 HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6048271
!Sample_status = Public on Jul 07 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 18 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Jul 07 2022
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: TCR: b chains
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Bulk
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B1
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor b chains
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Between 0.5-2.0 x106 PBMCs were pelleted and snap-frozen on dry-ice. Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from cell pellets.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.

!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.

!Sample_library_strategy = RNA-Seq
!Sample_supplementary_file_1 = ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/samples/GSM6048nnn/GSM6048286/suppl/GSM6048286_P30_B1_TCR_bulk_PBMC.tsv.gz
!Sample_series_id = GSE200996
!Sample_data_row_count = 0
^SAMPLE = GSM6048287
!Sample_title = P31 bulk TCR of B1 HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6048287
!Sample_status = Public on Jul 07 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 18 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Jul 07 2022
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: TCR: b chains
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Bulk
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B1
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor b chains
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Between 0.5-2.0 x106 PBMCs were pelleted and snap-frozen on dry-ice. Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from cell pellets.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Between 0.5-2.0 x106 PBMCs were pelleted and snap-frozen on dry-ice. Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from cell pellets.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.

!Sample_supplementary_file_1 = ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/samples/GSM6048nnn/GSM6048302/suppl/GSM6048302_P16_B2_TCR_bulk_PBMC.tsv.gz
!Sample_series_id = GSE200996
!Sample_data_row_count = 0
^SAMPLE = GSM6048303
!Sample_title = P17 bulk TCR of B2 HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6048303
!Sample_status = Public on Jul 07 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 18 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Jul 07 2022
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: TCR: b chains
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Bulk
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B2
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor b chains
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Between 0.5-2.0 x106 PBMCs were pelleted and snap-frozen on dry-ice. Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from cell pellets.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Between 0.5-2.0 x106 PBMCs were pelleted and snap-frozen on dry-ice. Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from cell pellets.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.

!Sample_supplementary_file_1 = ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/samples/GSM6048nnn/GSM6048318/suppl/GSM6048318_P04_B3_TCR_bulk_PBMC.tsv.gz
!Sample_series_id = GSE200996
!Sample_data_row_count = 0
^SAMPLE = GSM6048319
!Sample_title = P05 bulk TCR of B3 HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6048319
!Sample_status = Public on Jul 07 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 18 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Jul 07 2022
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: TCR: b chains
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Bulk
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B3
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor b chains
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Between 0.5-2.0 x106 PBMCs were pelleted and snap-frozen on dry-ice. Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from cell pellets.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Between 0.5-2.0 x106 PBMCs were pelleted and snap-frozen on dry-ice. Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from cell pellets.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.

!Sample_supplementary_file_1 = ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/samples/GSM6048nnn/GSM6048334/suppl/GSM6048334_P25_B3_TCR_bulk_PBMC.tsv.gz
!Sample_series_id = GSE200996
!Sample_data_row_count = 0
^SAMPLE = GSM6048335
!Sample_title = P27 bulk TCR of B3 HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6048335
!Sample_status = Public on Jul 07 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 18 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Jul 07 2022
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: TCR: b chains
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Bulk
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B3
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: T cell receptor b chains
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Between 0.5-2.0 x106 PBMCs were pelleted and snap-frozen on dry-ice. Bulk TCR sequencing was performed from DNA extracted from cell pellets.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Illumina libraries were prepared using the Adaptive Biotechnologies ImmunoSeq deep TCR beta assay.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Single cell
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B1
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: total RNA
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Frozen PBMC samples were sorted using T cell activation markers identified in scRNA-seq data. Cells were thawed in two groups (B1 or B2), diluted in FWB, and counted with a hemacytometer. Up to 5x106 cells were then centrifuged and resuspended in 1:500 Zombie Aqua (Biolegend) in PBS and incubated at RT for 15 minutes. Cells were resuspended in TruStainFx FcBlock (1:20 dilution) in FWB, incubated at 4°C for 15 minutes. Additional antibodies for sorting/analysis were then added Unique sample-specific hashtag TotalSeqC antibodies (Biolegend, #1-4) were added to each sample (10 uL per sample) for identification of cells from individual specimens. Cells were stained for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with FWB and filtered through a 40 um flow-cap strainer. Using a BD FACS Aria II instrument (BD Biosciences), live CD3+ CD4+ HLA-DR-high cells were sorted into PBS+BSA. Sorted cells were washed with 0.25% BSA and counted if numbers permitted (>30,000 cells). Cells from patient were pooled, using all sorted cells or up to 10,000 cells per patient. Each pool of cells was loaded into single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 assay protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX, feature barcode, and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)
!Sample_description = Hashtag_info_sorted_sc_GEX_PBMC.csv

!Sample_supplementary_file_1 = ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/samples/GSM6048nnn/GSM6048339/suppl/GSM6048339_raw_feature_bc_matrix_P13-P19-P26-P32_GEX_sc_sorted_B1_CD8_PBMC.h5
!Sample_series_id = GSE200996
!Sample_data_row_count = 0
^SAMPLE = GSM6048340
!Sample_title = P13, P19, P26 and P32 scRNA-seq of sorted B2 CD4+ HNSCC PBMC (Hashtag) 1
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6048340
!Sample_status = Public on Jul 07 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 18 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Jul 07 2022
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = HNSCC PBMC
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell marker: CD4+
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = single cell or bulk: Single cell
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = state: B2
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = patient diagnosis: Head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = molecule: total RNA
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Frozen PBMC samples were sorted using T cell activation markers identified in scRNA-seq data. Cells were thawed in two groups (B1 or B2), diluted in FWB, and counted with a hemacytometer. Up to 5x106 cells were then centrifuged and resuspended in 1:500 Zombie Aqua (Biolegend) in PBS and incubated at RT for 15 minutes. Cells were resuspended in TruStainFx FcBlock (1:20 dilution) in FWB, incubated at 4°C for 15 minutes. Additional antibodies for sorting/analysis were then added Unique sample-specific hashtag TotalSeqC antibodies (Biolegend, #1-4) were added to each sample (10 uL per sample) for identification of cells from individual specimens. Cells were stained for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with FWB and filtered through a 40 um flow-cap strainer. Using a BD FACS Aria II instrument (BD Biosciences), live CD3+ CD4+ HLA-DR-high cells were sorted into PBS+BSA. Sorted cells were washed with 0.25% BSA and counted if numbers permitted (>30,000 cells). Cells from patient were pooled, using all sorted cells or up to 10,000 cells per patient. Each pool of cells was loaded into single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 assay protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX, feature barcode, and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)
!Sample_description = Hashtag_info_sorted_sc_GEX_PBMC.csv
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

Using a BD FACS Aria II instrument (BD Biosciences), live CD3+ CD4+ HLA-DR-high cells were sorted into PBS+BSA. Sorted cells were washed with 0.25% BSA and counted if numbers permitted (>30,000 cells). Cells from patient were pooled, using all sorted cells or up to 10,000 cells per patient. Each pool of cells was loaded into single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 assay protocol.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Libraries were prepared accordingn to 10X Genomics protocols for 5' barcoded GEX, feature barcode, and V(D)J TCR (Version 1)
!Sample_data_processing = Raw PBMC scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed and aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A from 10x Genomics) for each pooled library using Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). Each pooled library contained multiple patient samples and timepoints; cells from each sample were labelled with distinct Hashtag oligonucleotides (HTO, Cell Hashing). Sequencing files for Gene Expression (measure mRNA level of cells) and Antibody Capture (measure HTO levels of cells) were fed to the “cellranger count” function with the –libraries flag, and the sequences of all HTO used in the library were fed to this function with –feature-ref flag. This generated a digital gene expression matrix, which measured the number of unique molecular identifier (UMI) for each gene and each cell barcode.
!Sample_data_processing = The raw gene-by-barcode count matrix was then processed to filter potential empty drops using emptyDrops function from DropletUtils (v1.8.0, R package) (Lun et al., 2019) with the parameters of “lower = 500, ignore = 5”. We initially selected droplets as containing a cell if total UMI counts of this droplet exceed the 99th percentile of the top 10,000 barcodes divided by 10. Finally, only cells with FDR<=0.01 were retained as real cells for the following analysis. The raw HTO-by-barcode matrix was subsequently filtered based on identified real cells.
!Sample_data_processing = The filtered HTO-by-barcode matrix for each pooled library was processed using GMM-demux to distinguish singlets from doublets or multiplets based on detection of HTOs with default parameters (Xin et al., 2020). Predicted singlets with a confidence score>=0.8 were defined as true singlet cells. Cell barcodes were then classified and allocated to respective patient samples based on hashtag identities. After processing, the gene-by-barcode count matrix was refined based on these identified singlets and used for the following analyses.
!Sample_data_processing = Raw tumor scRNA-sequencing reads were demultiplexed to FASTQ files using Cell Ranger mkfastq (v3.0.0, 10x Genomics), and the Cumulus cellranger-workflow implementation of Cell Ranger count (v4.0.0) on Terra (https://terra.bio/) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38-2020-A) and generate a raw counts matrix (Li et al., 2020). Cumulus was used to filter cells from the Cell Ranger raw counts matrix with fewer than 400 UMIs, 200 genes, or greater than 20% of UMIs mapped to mitochondrial genes.
!Sample_data_processing = To generate the single-cell V(D)J sequences and annotate each library, we aligned TCR FASTQ reads to human GRCh38 V(D)J reference (v4.0.0 from 10X Genomics, modified to remove TRDD segments) using “cellranger vdj” function from Cell Ranger (v4.0.0). The filtered contig annotations, which contained high-level annotations of each high-confident cellular contig, were further filtered by removing records with ‘raw_consensus_id’ as ‘none’. For blood single-cell V(D)J analysis, the identities of different patient samples in each pooled library were labelled based on demultiplexing of the gene expression matrix.
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: Each scRNA sequenting sample contains a .h5 file including Gene Expression (tumor and PBMC) and Antibody Capture (PBMC) information. Single cell TCR sequencing data for each sample were saved in a csv file, which is generated by 'cellranger vdj' function and shows the detailed clonotype information. Bulk TCR sequencing data for each sample were provided by Adaptive Biotech and were saved in a tsv file. Hashtag files contain the sequence of each hashtag and the corresponding patient sample information.

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Frozen PBMC samples were sorted using T cell activation markers identified in scRNA-seq data. Cells were thawed in two groups (B1 or B2), diluted in FWB, and counted with a hemacytometer. Up to 5x106 cells were then centrifuged and resuspended in 1:500 Zombie Aqua (Biolegend) in PBS and incubated at RT for 15 minutes. Cells were resuspended in TruStainFx FcBlock (1:20 dilution) in FWB, incubated at 4°C for 15 minutes. Additional antibodies for sorting/analysis were then added Unique sample-specific hashtag TotalSeqC antibodies (Biolegend, #1-4) were added to each sample (10 uL per sample) for identification of cells from individual specimens. Cells were stained for 20 minutes at 4°C, washed twice with FWB and filtered through a 40 um flow-cap strainer. Using a BD FACS Aria II instrument (BD Biosciences), live CD3+ CD8+ CD38+HLA-DR+ cells were sorted into PBS+BSA. Sorted cells were washed with 0.25% BSA and counted if numbers permitted (>30,000 cells). Cells from patient were pooled, using all sorted cells or up to 10,000 cells per patient. Each pool of cells was loaded into single Chip A channel, along with the reverse transcriptase reagent mixture and 5’ gel beads according to the 10x Genomics 5’ V1 assay protocol.
